summary: The tab scroll-restore journey asserts a cross-tab inequality instead of an exact offset, so it can pass for the wrong reason or fail when both tabs clamp to the same scroll extent.
evidence: cmd/goosie/journey_p1_tabs_test.go:96-105 presses PageDown twice in tab 2 and waits for active.ScrollY() > tab1Scroll, comparing one tab's offset against a different tab's; the same test then asserts exact equality (== tab1Scroll, == tab2Scroll) at lines 121 and 132. The inequality oracle depends on page heights and clamp values, and it is the assertion that failed twice under machine load. Re-measured 2026-10-26 on 6071b8b: 3 failures in 45 iterations of -race runs (-count=5: 1, -count=8: 1, -count=8: 0, -count=24: 1) and in the -count=24 run the failure was the FIRST iteration of a freshly built test binary while the 23 later iterations each took 0.16s and passed - the failing one spent its 8.12s inside this wait, so cold-start load is the trigger, not random scheduling. Two candidate mechanisms were measured and dismissed: (i) surface.mergeEvent folding two PageDown presses into one - a burst of four bare pressKey injections with no wait produced exactly four pages (one page 432, burst total 2160), so at steady state discrete keys are not lost; (ii) scrollContentTo computing the target from the shared scheduler viewport while ScrollY is per-tab - in 20/20 -race runs tab 2's ScrollY equalled sched.Viewport().Offset.Y at both steps (432/432 then 864/864). Replacing the second press with a wheel delta made the test fail 30/30, which is registered on its own as GOOSIE-WHEEL-001, so the oracle stays as written and the mechanism that parks tab 2 at tab 1's offset on a cold binary stays unidentified.

summary: On nine real web pages Goosie lays out nothing, or paints a handful of pixels, and still exits 0 with an empty stderr - the user gets a blank window and the engine records no reason anywhere.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-001. Measured by testdata/live-parity.py against Chromium/Playwright at viewport 1280x1024, dpr 1, wait_until=load, screenshots viewport-only on both sides. Source: docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json (94 of 100 pages comparable). Eight pages have doc_height=0 AND ink_goosie=0 with goosie_rc=0 and an empty goosie_diag: apnews.com (Chromium painted 15,805 ink px), www.nytimes.com (68,129), www.japantimes.co.jp (17,749), www.reuters.com (13,145), www.etsy.com (16,539), www.newegg.com (17,467), www.zara.com (8,846), www.gov.vn (501,735). vnexpress.net is a different shape of the same silence: doc_height=691 but ink_goosie=32 against ink_chromium=301,440. All nine carry the identical label in the earlier run (2026-10-25T1630Z) as well, so this is not load noise; of the 6 label changes between the runs none is in this family (www.usatoday.com was LAYOUT_EMPTY at run 1 and LOW_COVERAGE at run 2, so it is deliberately not counted here). Offline probes on saved copies of the served HTML prove this is at least two distinct causes, not one: www.gov.vn reproduces with no network (curl-saved 192,815-byte document whose decoded text carries 11,859 visible characters across 177,201 body characters, served with 26 inline <script> tags) and ./bin/goosie -screenshot on that file yields rc 0, ink 0, while -gate -frames 120 reports doc_height=0, tiles_rasterized=0, zero_work_frames=120 - the frame path ran 120 frames with no document to draw. apnews.com does NOT reproduce offline: the same command on its saved 2,610,822-byte copy (70,685 visible characters) paints 763,855 ink px at doc_height=34,867, so the live failure of that page must come from the fetch/response path rather than from layout of the markup. (www.gov.vn is also the only page in this family whose corpus expect is 'static'; the other seven are 'js-revealed'.) Caveat for whoever investigates: style_passes and layout_passes read 0 on both runs, including on apnews where layout clearly succeeded, so those two counters are frame-window figures and must not be cited as evidence that styling never ran. Nothing distinguishes any of these from a page that genuinely has nothing to draw: the -screenshot path exits 0, so neither CI nor a user can tell. Not root-caused further - TASK-038 §4 forbids engine changes in a measurement task. TASK-039 SPLIT (measured 2026-10-26, docs/tasks/TASK-039-LIVE-PAGE-NO-OUTPUT.md §5.7): the family is six branches, not one. Three now have fixes on main - the refusal status line (branch A: a source that answers 4xx used to be painted as an ordinary page with no note), `nodeType` in the JS binding (branch B: a Sizzle-shaped `9 === doc.nodeType` gate that never passed, so the setup script died before revealing content; oracle BR-188), and uncaught-exception recording (branch E: BR-189/BR-190, so a page that broke now says so on stderr). Three stay open: branch C (missing Node/DOM APIs - `createDocumentFragment`/`insertBefore` completion), branch D (paced modes never install `setTick`, so `PumpJS` never runs and JS-revealed content cannot appear in a `-screenshot`/`-gate`/`-bench` run), and branch F (the corner ink artefact, GOOSIE-LIVE-006). One page in the family did move: vnexpress.net went from ink_goosie=32 (BLANK_OUTPUT) to 320,348 (LOW_COVERAGE) between the da68c5b and eef92ae sweeps - attributed offline on one saved copy to the CSS string-state fix, see GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-002, and NOT to any TASK-039 branch. CORRECTION (2026-10-26, integrator): the vnexpress.net movement from ink_goosie=32 to 320,348 between the da68c5b and eef92ae sweeps is real, but the sentence appended above attributing it to 'the CSS string-state fix repaired the sheet' is falsified by a direct measurement - see GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-003: on vnexpress's own second inline stylesheet the eef92ae parser loses a tail rule that da68c5b keeps (marker ink 0 vs 14,400). The page-level improvement therefore comes from a different sheet on the page, and the branch is still open for this site (LOW_COVERAGE, coverage 0.441). summary: A legal custom property name that begins with digits (--8e8e8e) is mistaken for an oversized geometry dimension, so the whole document is refused: cafef.vn gets no window, and the message names no property, no value and no limit.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-002. Reproduced offline with no network from a saved copy: ./bin/goosie -screenshot -url file:///tmp/cafef.html (217,170 bytes) exits 1 and writes exactly one stderr line, 'goosie: goosie: build session: CSS numeric value outside safe geometry range' (the prefix is doubled). The live sweep labels it ADMISSION_CAPPED in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json; in the earlier run it was GOOSIE_CRASH, the same family mislabelled before the ladder put a refusal check ahead of the exit-code check. ROOT CAUSE, measured by bisection and not yet fixed: document -> 9 <style> blocks (dropping them clears the refusal; dropping style= attributes does not) -> block 8 of 36 rules -> one rule, '.box-ttdn .list .mdn .time { color: var(--8e8e8e, #8e8e8e); ... }'. The one-line repro is ':root{--8e8e8e:#8e8e8e}' and '.a{color:var(--8e8e8e)}'. The name of that custom property begins with digits, so the tokenizer reads 8e8 as a scientific number and then swallows the following 'e8' as a unit, producing a Dimension token worth 800,000,000; internal/engine/limits.go:239-241 applies MaxGeometry = 2<<20 (2,097,152) to dimensions and percentages, and the document is refused. A variant matrix measured on this host confirms the mechanism exactly: ':root{--8e8:1}' rc 0 (plain number, cap deliberately skipped), ':root{--8e8e8:1}' rc 1, ':root{--1e9e9:1}' rc 1, ':root{--8e5e5:1}' rc 0 (800,000 under the cap), ':root{--1e2e2:1}' rc 0, ':root{--abc8e8e8:1}' rc 0 (ident, no number token), '.a{width:8e8}' rc 0, '.a{width:8e8e8px}' rc 1 (a genuine dimension, correctly refused). Chromium, measured with Playwright on the same minimal document, resolves var(--8e8e8e) to rgb(171, 205, 239): a custom property name that begins with digits is legal and contains no number at all, so this refusal is a false positive that blanks an entire news site - renaming the one ident to --grey makes the saved cafef document render at rc 0 with 554,999 ink pixels. Hypotheses already disproved on this document: replacing every 7-or-more-digit number (including z-index:999999999) does not clear the refusal, because the trigger is an 8-character ident with no run of digits; and the document loads no external stylesheet, so linked CSS is not involved. Compounding the damage, the same coarse message is emitted from three sites - internal/engine/limits.go:226 (float64 overflow), :231 (non-finite), :241 (magnitude) - and none names the property, the value, or the bound, unlike :249 'CSS declaration limit exceeded (%d)'. CLOSED, re-measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 rather than accepted on the implementer's report. Fix is in the tokenizer, not the guard: internal/css/token.go now orders the U+002D branch as 4.3.11 (a hyphen reaches readNumber only before a digit, or a '.' and a digit) then 4.3.10 (a second hyphen or an ident-start code point makes it an ident) then Delim, so --8e8e8e is one ident and MaxGeometry stays 2<<20 (TestMaxGeometryIsUnchanged pins the constant). Live page measured on this host at 1280x800 with the two binaries side by side: main at 2ca7889 gives rc 1, no PNG, stderr 'goosie: goosie: build session: CSS numeric value outside safe geometry range'; the branch binary gives rc 0, PNG 84,760 B, 1,004,804 ink pixels. Mutation proof on the merged tree: restoring the old dispatch kills TestHyphenTokenKind (6 sub-cases incl. -webkit-mask and --a(), i.e. vendor prefixes and custom-property functions were also being mis-tokenised), TestDigitLeadingCustomPropertyRefusalMatrix (7 sub-cases), TestDigitLeadingCustomPropertyPaints, TestGoosieDigitLeadingCustomPropertyIsAdmitted (exit status 1) and the parity gate itself (fixture render missing, 84/85, exit 1). Restoring the old content-free refusal sentence kills TestGeometryRefusalNamesEverything (both branches, per-field fail lines) and TestGoosieGeometryRefusalLineIsWellFormed; restoring 'goosie:', err kills only the process-level oracle - cmd/goosie's two unit tests stay green under that mutation, which is disclosed rather than fixed, because the line an operator reads is what carries the claim. Left unfixed on purpose and still open in behaviour: (1) '+' and '.' still go straight to readNumber without the spec's 'check if three code points would start a number', so a '.' not followed by a digit is not read as a delimiter - consequence not measured, so no new defect id is claimed here; (2) the guard's non-finite branch is unreachable from any token the tokenizer emits, so its message has no behavioural oracle; (3) escapes inside ident sequences are still not consumed, so --\-foo is not the ident the spec describes (GOOSIE-CSSSELECT-001 family). Registry: BR-192 (tokenizer dispatch, INT+PARITY) and BR-193 (geometry guard and its refusal message, SEC+INT) cover the contract; fixture testdata/render/css-features/11-digit-leading-custom-property.html scored 98.90% PASS, corpus 85/85 at average 96.16%, floor 84 -> 85, tagged-case ratchet 73 -> 75.
closed_by: 4278104 (tokenizer dispatch) + a8266ff (refusal message) + 09d1874 (single program label)

summary: The parity scorer can grade a page 'OK' while Goosie's ink sits almost nowhere near Chromium's: coverage is an ink-mass ratio that rises above 1, and the positional score (worst_iou) is recorded but never consulted.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-004 - a defect in the measuring infrastructure, not in the engine. coverage comes from parity.score_regions (testdata/parity.py:279): goosie_total / chromium_total, so it exceeds 1 whenever Goosie paints more ink than the reference. 30 of the 94 comparable pages in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json report coverage > 1.0, up to 2.83 (www.w3.org/Style/CSS/, 1,306,325 Goosie ink px vs 15,209 Chromium), 2.57 (ebay.com, 1,228,884 vs 94,816), 2.32 (validator.w3.org). Worse, the label ignores position: among the 46 OK pages, 26 have worst_iou < 0.5 and 16 have worst_iou < 0.1, including en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam (coverage 1.547, worst_iou 0.001, 0 of 4 bands blank) and wiki/Cuneiform (1.972, 0.014). grep of testdata/live-parity.py shows worst_iou is written at :162 (now :214) and never read by classify - re-checked after TASK-045: classify still contains no worst_iou or pct_exact test, those values are only surfaced through MEASURED_KEYS (:155) and the per-row note (:269). Written on 2026-10-25 as: 'blank-band and dimension checks are position-sensitive, so LAYOUT_EMPTY, BLANK_OUTPUT, MISSING_REGIONS and DIMENSION_MISMATCH stay trustworthy'. That half is now falsified for BLANK_OUTPUT: measured on 2026-10-26 at 452b6c2, a band reported blank can hold Goosie's line ~20px away (GOOSIE-BLANKMETRIC-001), so BLANK_OUTPUT does not by itself prove content is absent. LAYOUT_EMPTY, MISSING_REGIONS and DIMENSION_MISMATCH are unaffected by that measurement and still stand. What is missing is a positional criterion that separates 'content absent' from 'content elsewhere'. Disclosed rather than retuned: LIVE_COVERAGE_OK = 0.60 and MIN_SCORED = 75 were fixed before the first run and never adjusted afterwards (TASK-038 §6.5). Sweep 2026-10-25T2045Z-ec0f7fb9 (100 pages, 93 scored) sizes the OK-labeled half directly: of its 44 OK rows, 17 report pct_exact below 50, the worst being www.target.com at 0.24, w3.org/Style/CSS/ 0.63, tuoitre.vn 0.84, plo.vn 1.96, nld.com.vn 3.6 and ebay.com 6.4 - every one of them 'green' in the label table; 28 of all rows report coverage above 1.0. classify (testdata/live-parity.py:222, at :171-212 before TASK-045 moved it) has no rung for 'measured, and the pixels disagree', so a page with 0.24% exact match falls through to OK as long as it has ink, no blank band and coverage >= 0.6. Any statement about live parity therefore has to be made in pct_exact, not in label counts, until a positional rung exists. Still open after TASK-045 (merged ca39672), but two facts changed and are recorded so nobody reads them as a fix: the ladder's terminal rung is renamed from `OK` to `UNFLAGGED` (testdata/live-parity.py:124, feeding LADDER at :140 and SCORED_LABELS at :147 and the exit code) precisely because this entry shows 'OK' was a goodness word attached to pages with 0.24% exact pixels, and every row now carries pct_exact and worst_iou into the markdown table and the terminal-labelled page list. The substance of this defect - classify has no rung for 'measured, and the pixels disagree' - is untouched: a page at pct_exact 0.24 still falls through to the terminal rung, it is just honestly named now. Consequence for the sweep series: label-to-label diffs across the boundary need the mapping `OK` (sweeps #1-#5) = `UNFLAGGED` (sweep #6 onward), and no committed report yet carries the new label, so the first table containing it will be sweep #6. Sweep #6 (`2026-10-25T2212Z-4302e3cb`, source 9754fda4, first report in the new vocabulary) repeats the pattern under the honest name: 43 rows carry `UNFLAGGED` and **14 of them report `pct_exact` below 50**, the worst being www.target.com 0.24, w3.org/Style/CSS/ 0.63, aljazeera.com 0.99, baomoi.com 5.64, ebay.com 6.39, dw.com 16.47 - the terminal rung is still reached by pixels that almost entirely disagree, because classify still has no positional rung. Same sweep moves the two numbers the floor is measured on: 95 of 100 pages scored (floor 75, met) and a noise pass of 12 sites whose max |delta_pct_exact| fell to 4.64 with **0 label flips**, against sweep 5's 18.36 with 4 flips on identical-ish code - so the reference side calmed down, and GOOSIE-LIVE-008's reopen shows why that comparison is only trustworthy read from the JSON `build` block.

summary: A 'blank band' in the parity metric can mean 'Goosie painted that line 20px away', not 'content missing', so the known-gaps baseline counts and TASK-027's band classification are not evidence about features.
evidence: testdata/parity.py:253-279 score_regions(): bands come from content_bands(cm) on the Chromium mask only, and a band is reported blank when goosie_count == 0 inside Chromium's exact rows. The IoU path dilates by one row (_dilate_one) before comparing; the blank test does not dilate at all, so a line that is present but shifted by more than the band's own gap registers as absent. Two measured instances on 2026-10-26 at 452b6c2. selectors/03-pseudo-elements band (457,475): Goosie has ink rows 437-455 and 483-498 and none between, and the crop shows the paragraph and its checkmark painted. layout-features/05-floats band (1055,1071): both the current build and a build with the float skip removed paint the sentence, about 15px apart, yet one reports 0 ink in the band and the other 2,289. Blast radius: testdata/render-known-gaps.json stores 5 fixtures / 10 bands and is the release-gate baseline; docs/tasks/TASK-027-GLYPH-COVERAGE.md 6 classified those bands by cause, and at least three of them are now known to be artifacts; testdata/live-parity.py imports score_regions by reference, so every live row inherits the same meaning of BLANK_OUTPUT. Fix direction, without touching any threshold: report a drift-adjusted blank - search Goosie ink in a window of +-band height around the Chromium rows and label 'shifted' separately from 'absent' - then re-classify the 10 declared bands from the new column. LIVE_COVERAGE_OK, PASS_AT, THRESHOLD and MIN_INK stay frozen; this adds a signal, it does not loosen one. MERGED STATE, re-measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 at fc15c19 rather than taken from the branch: score_regions_drift landed as a report-only second view; scoring the SAME 82 renders with main and with the branch produced ZERO field differences across all 82 fixtures (match_pct, status, blank_regions, blank_region_rows, coverage_ratio, worst_region_iou) and the summary stayed 82/82 at average 96.088% with known gaps 5 fixtures / 10 bands. On the corpus the split is 10 declared blank bands -> 9 shifted, 1 truly_blank (html-features/01-forms-complete.png rows 593-599: zero ink inside the +-7 window, nearest ink 8 rows away). Three mutations were run and reverted here, not quoted: drift window = 0 reddens the selftest case that expects a shifted band, window x40 reddens case D3 (ink painted 100 rows away) so the width is load-bearing rather than tuned, and redefining the OLD signal inside score_regions - instead of adding a side result - makes `make parity` exit 1 on the known-gap equality. render-known-gaps.json is deliberately NOT re-baselined to 1: blank_regions keeps its original meaning, so declaring one band would loosen the gate under cover of a reclassification. BR-187 carries the oracle (test/gatecheck/parity_harness_test.go:TestParityDriftMetricIsGreen plus selftest cases D1-D4); the ratchet was re-measured, not assumed: P0 tagged 19, P0/P1 tagged 69, unchanged, because BR-187 is P2. WHAT STILL KEEPS THIS OPEN: the drift column exists only for the fixture corpus. The live sweep's 25 MISSING_REGIONS rows are still graded by the un-adjusted band count, and TASK-042 could not measure their drift share because live-parity.py writes its PNGs into a temp dir and shutil.rmtree removes them when it exits (live-parity.py:679,688) - so the number everyone will ask for, 'how many of the 25 are displacement', is still unknown, and the sweep's own label for a whole-page blank (BLANK_OUTPUT, 1 page, vnexpress at 32 ink px) is structurally NOT drift: with page-wide ink below LIVE_MIN_INK no band can reach MIN_INK in any window. MEASURED ON THE LIVE SIDE (2026-10-26, docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1920Z-eef92ae7.json): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat is labelled MISSING_REGIONS with 1 blank band at rows [98,119] while Goosie's total ink is 215,401 against Chromium's 216,818 - 0.65% less, over a 23,269 px document. A page that paints 99.35% of the reference's ink and is called 'missing regions' is exactly the confusion this defect is about, and live-parity.py cannot yet separate shifted from truly blank because it deletes both PNGs after scoring (testdata/live-parity.py:679,688). The parity-side split is shipped (BR-187); the live-side split is the remaining half.

summary: Render parity is only ever measured on one host: the CI parity job on ubuntu-latest fails 14 of 80 fixtures while this macOS host scores 81 of 81, so a green `make parity` is evidence about a machine, not about the engine.
evidence: Discovered while closing GOOSIE-PARITYGATE-001, from CI's own artifact, not from a local run. The last three CI runs of the job 'Render parity vs Chromium' all concluded failure: 39990406790 (2026-10-23), 40069270435 and 40107385303 (2026-10-24). Newest artifact (run 40107385303, job 120911782700, head c8cd80b, ubuntu-latest, playwright==1.49.1): summary total 80, passing 66, failing 14, errors 0, avg_match_pct 93.638 at threshold 30 / pass_at 90.0. Same corpus on this macOS host at e310f55: 81/81 passing, avg 96.09%. The 14 CI failures are html-features/02 89.9, typography/09 89.62, overflow/01 89.28, typography/06 88.78, layout-features/01 88.76, typography/04 88.65, edge-cases/02 88.37, colors/02 87.19, tables/03 87.08, edge-cases/01 87.08, tables/02 86.39, positioning/03 83.95, selectors/01 81.64, colors/01 80.33. Two structural readings of that list, both measured: 0 dimension mismatches across all 80 rows (goosie_size == chromium_size in every row), so the pages are comparable shapes and the disagreement is pixels only; and the CI pass band starts at 90.364 while the worst failure is 89.9 - the verdict for 17% of the corpus sits within 0.46 points of the pass line, i.e. the gate is a cliff, not a slope. Hypothesis, NOT tested: Linux font rasterisation shifts text enough to move those 14 rows under PASS_AT, because no same-commit A/B exists - CI has never run at the current head and this host never scored c8cd80b. Why it must not be waved away: TASK-036 turned the known-gaps baseline into an exact ratchet, so render-known-gaps.json (5 fixtures / 10 bands) is now host-specific, and on another host a shifted band becomes 'known-gap baseline is stale' FAIL rather than a silent pass; whether that actually bites on Linux is unknowable from the artifact, because per-region scoring did not exist at c8cd80b (grep -c blank_regions on that revision's parity.py = 0) and the report therefore carries no iou, coverage or band columns at all. Needed, in order: one ubuntu-latest run of the current head with --render --render-chromium, its parity.json archived; then either a per-platform baseline file or a recorded decision that Linux CI is the authority for this gate; then re-examine whether a 90.0 pass_at is defensible when the host spread alone can cross it. Separately, the same run's 'Race detector' job also failed, so BR-179's 'go test ./..., go vet, archtest and the gate suite all exit 0 on the candidate commit' is currently unmet on CI for reasons unrelated to parity - unmeasured here, since the failure log for that job was not pulled. CORRECTION to 'needs a Linux host': module-graph questions ARE measurable on this machine via GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go list (that is how GOOSIE-LICENSE-001 was proven), but PIXEL questions are not - no container runtime exists here (docker, podman, colima all absent), so the 14 CI failures cannot be reproduced or dismissed locally, and the only route to a Linux render is a CI run, which needs a push the user has not authorised. PARTIAL 2026-11-12, landed in a7012b40, without a single new Linux number. What changed is that the next ubuntu-latest run can be read: `testdata/render-known-gaps.json` now carries `measured_on: "darwin"`, `parity.py` exposes `known_gap_provenance()` (no parameter on purpose - it reads the `KNOWN_GAPS` global at call time, because `def load_known_gaps(path=KNOWN_GAPS)` binds its default at def-time and a parameterised accessor would answer about a file the caller is not using), `main()` prints a stderr NOTE naming both hosts whenever they differ - and stating the one cure it forbids, editing the baseline to match the verdict - and the JSON report carries `metadata.known_gaps_provenance {file, measured_on, host_platform, matches_host}`, so an archived report says which baseline its verdict was compared against. The CI parity job renders BOTH sides into a per-run `--workdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/parity"`, writes `--diffs`, and uploads parity.json/junit/diffs with `if: always()` - run 40107385303 could list 14 failing fixtures and still not show what a single one looked like. Oracles: `parity_selftest.py` case 9 (7 checks; 48 green overall) + gate `test/gatecheck/parity_harness_test.go:TestParityBaselineRecordsItsHost` (qc:BR-265, catalog row BR-265, `expectedCaseCount` 264 -> 265). The gate deliberately does NOT assert `measured_on == runtime.GOOS`: the mismatch is the condition being named, and pinning it would turn an honest NOTE into a red gate. Measured mutants, each restored: deleting `measured_on` from the real file turns case 9's last check red and a full local run prints "an unrecorded platform" once, so an unlabelled baseline is reported rather than assumed to be the host measuring it; printing the NOTE unconditionally turns the same-host check red; making the accessor return `... or sys.platform` turns two checks red; renaming the key in the file turns the gate red. Blast radius on this host: `python3 testdata/parity.py --render --binary ./goosie` -> 107/107, avg 96.43%, gaps 4 fixtures / 6 bands, rc 0, `matches_host: true`; `go vet -all ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go test ./internal/archtest/` all rc 0. What this defect still needs, in the same order: (1) one ubuntu-latest run of the current head - blocked, it needs a push the user has not authorised, and pixel questions are not measurable here (no docker, podman, colima, qemu-x86_64); (2) a baseline measured on Linux, now expressible as data rather than as a decision about who owns a single file - the protocol, and the explicit ban on copying darwin's numbers to match a verdict, are in `docs/tasks/TASK-036-PARITY-HARNESS-FAIL-CLOSED.md` §10; (3) re-examining `PASS_AT = 90.0` against the measured host spread (the CI pass band began at 90.364% and the worst failure was 89.900%), which stays a judgement call until (1) exists.

summary: The distribution-provenance gate could not pass on both build hosts while it read the host's own go list - RESOLVED in code by BR-194 (per-target audit, merged 0cefc1d), but no non-darwin artifact has ever been executed and CI is still not measured green, so the provenance of the shipped binaries is not yet closed.
evidence: Gate 8 (test/gatecheck/licenses_test.go TestLinkedDependenciesPinned) is the only evidence for the licence provenance of the shipped binaries, and it enforces two directions: every linked module must be pinned (:70) and every pinned module must be linked (:78-82). go list -deps is target-dependent, so the two directions contradict each other across platforms and NO allowlist content can satisfy both. Measured at 32e3409 on this darwin/arm64 host without any Linux machine, because GOOS/GOARCH are honoured by go list: `go list -f '{{if not .Standard}}{{.Module.Path}}@{{.Module.Version}}{{end}}' -deps ./cmd/goosie ./cmd/goosie-headless | sort -u` yields 7 modules (regexp2/v2 v2.5.2, goja, sourcemap, pprof, x/image v0.45.0, x/net v0.60.0, x/text v0.42.0) with no x/sys, while the same command under GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 yields 8, adding golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0 (chain: go mod why -m golang.org/x/sys -> x/image/font/opentype -> x/image/vector -> x/sys/cpu; x/image/vector IS linked on darwin too - grep -c gives 1 - so the delta is precisely the x/sys/cpu leaf). Both directions of the trap were run, not inferred: CI's own log for run 40107385303 job 120911782481 at head c8cd80b says 'licenses_test.go:71: linked module golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0 is not in dependency-licenses.txt (re-audit and amend)' and that is the ONLY test failure in that job (no DATA RACE line anywhere in it, so the job title is misleading), while appending exactly that line here and re-running produced 'licenses_test.go:80: allowlist entry golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0 is linked into no release binary (stale pin?)' -> FAIL, after which the file was restored and the test went ok again. Consequence for the release DoD: BR-179 ('go test ./..., go vet -all ./..., archtest and the gate suite all exit 0 on the candidate commit') is unmet on CI for this single cause, and it has been unmet for the last three runs (39990406790, 40069270435, 40107385303). The licence itself is not the problem: /Users/vyquocvu/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0/LICENSE is the standard Go BSD-3-Clause text (Copyright 2009 The Go Authors; three conditions including the no-endorsement clause; ALL WARRANTIES disclaimer), already inside the permitted set, and the directory's PATENTS file is golang's standard grant, not copyleft. What is owed is a target-aware contract: declare the release target list in code, pin the union of modules across those targets, and judge staleness only against modules absent from EVERY target - plus a table-driven oracle so this fails on any laptop before CI does. summary: The TASK-041 bad-string fix treated every newline inside a quoted CSS string as the line break that ends it, including an escaped one (`\` + newline), so real stylesheets that split a long quoted value across two lines lost that declaration AND the rest of the sheet: doc.rust-lang.org/std/ dropped from 95,783 ink px to 53,215. No committed gate could see it.
evidence: Mechanism: f5cec79 (the commit that closed GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-001) added `closesStringAt(quote, c) { return c == quote || c == '\n' }` and wired it into three scanners - parseRule's selector loop, parseRule's declaration-body loop, and parseBlockWithRules' statement loop - with no handling of the backslash that escapes the next byte. CSS Syntax L3 4.3.7 makes a RAW newline end an open string as a bad-string, but 4.3.8 makes `\` + newline a valid escape *inside* the token. rustdoc's generated CSS ends five lines (6/54/61/65/68 of its main sheet) with `\` inside `url("data:image/svg+xml,…")`, so Goosie cut the string, ate the `;`, dropped the declaration, and lost every rule after it in that sheet. Ground truth measured on Chromium/Playwright 131.x on this host, four shapes, all in TASK-041 §7.1: escaped `url()` keeps 2 rules with `background-image` computed to `url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='a'%3E%3C/svg%3E")` and the image loading; escaped `font-family` computes to `GoosieSerif`; a RAW newline keeps 1 rule with 0 declarations and computed colour black; an escaped newline in an attribute selector yields 2 rules with selectorText `a[title="xy"]` and the following `.z` still applying. Pre-fix Goosie scored 0 declarations, 0 declarations, 0 declarations (already correct) and 1 merged rule respectively. Real-page effect, same canvas 1280x1024 dpr 1, metric parity.ink_mask: 4de0fca 95,783 px / 23 content bands, da68c5b (TASK-041 merged) 53,215 px / 16 bands, after the fix 95,814 px / 23 bands. On the minimal probe /tmp/escprobe/escaped-newline.html at 800x600 the fixed build's PNG is md5-identical to the 4de0fca PNG (c47c831b9f4889fa31eaa3ca127364f9) - green 40,000 / red 40,000 px vs the regression's 0 / 0 / 445 ink. WHY NO GATE SAW IT, which is the part worth keeping: `make parity` reported 81/81 passing at average 96.09% both before and after the regression shipped, because no fixture in testdata/render contained an escaped newline; the unit oracle in test/css covered four raw-newline shapes and no backslash; and a SAVED copy of the same rustdoc page renders identically on both binaries (51,939 px / 17 bands) because the escaped CSS only arrives on a fresh fetch - so the offline A/B that validated TASK-041 was blind by construction. The only thing that caught it was the 100-site live sweep (docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1845Z-da68c5bc.json), which is evidence for the sweep being a gate and not a report. Fixed in a9f6218: the three scanners skip the byte after a backslash while a string is open, and stripEscapedNewlines removes `\` + line-break pairs from inside quoted values the way Chromium computes them, leaving `\2014`, `\A` and Windows paths untouched. Proofs measured: (M1) reverting internal/css/parser.go makes the new fixture css-features/09-escaped-newline-string.html score 84.87% FAIL with blank_regions 2/0 rows [(295,310),(425,452)], 81/82 passing, parity exit 1; (M2) deleting only the stripEscapedNewlines call reddens exactly one assertion - and the fixture stays green at 96.24%, so the value-unescape half is guarded by the unit oracle ONLY, stated plainly rather than assumed; (M3) the raw-newline control branch of TestEscapedNewlineVersusRawNewline was green before the fix and stays green after it, so nothing was loosened. Still open in this family, recorded not hidden: escaped QUOTES (`content:"a\"b"`) still close the string at the five scanners this change did not touch (parser.go :1321, :1346, :1419, :1681, :1784 and SplitDeclarations), which is the same debt §6 of TASK-041 already logged for stripComments and readString; and Goosie keeps the escape pair verbatim in selector text (`a[title="x\<NL>y"]`) where Chromium serialises `a[title="xy"]`. BR-186 now carries 9 tests and its measured row names both defects.

summary: A Content-Type sent with a comma instead of a semicolon (`text/html, charset=UTF-8`) is not recognised as a displayable type, so Goosie treats the response as a download: the page never paints and -screenshot exits 1 with no PNG while Chromium renders the same bytes.
evidence: Found by the 100-site live sweep at da68c5b, on https://www.target.com/s/coffee (label changed OK -> FETCH_FAILED-class, then proven to be neither network nor a Goosie regression). Root cause: internal/download/download.go:21 ShouldDownload strips parameters with `strings.IndexByte(ct, ';')` only, so the header value `text/html, charset=UTF-8` lowercases to `text/html, charset=utf-8`, matches none of the four whitelisted cases, and falls through to `default: return true` - download it. RFC 9110 §8.3 puts parameters after `;`, so the comma form is a server-side bug, but a browser is the party that has to cope and Chromium does. Measured offline, not argued: /tmp/ctprobe/serve.py replays the exact response bytes the site sends (429 status, `Content-Type: text/html, charset=UTF-8`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, the challenge body); against that single server Goosie exits 1 and writes no PNG while Playwright/Chromium renders the body. Pre-existing, not caused by the CSS work: `git diff 4de0fca HEAD -- internal/net internal/download` is empty. Blast radius measured so far is one URL in the 100-site corpus; the shape is common enough (429 challenge pages served with a hand-built header) that the honest description is 'unknown until swept again'. What closing it needs: parameter parsing that splits on ';' and trims, a table-driven oracle in test/download covering `text/html`, `text/html;charset=utf-8`, `text/html; charset=utf-8`, `text/html, charset=UTF-8`, `application/xhtml+xml`, and a genuinely downloadable `application/pdf; charset=binary`; plus a user-visible consequence - a -screenshot run whose answer was routed to the downloader must say so on stderr instead of exiting 1 silently, which is the same class as GOOSIE-LIVE-003 (a run that gave up looks like a run that succeeded).

summary: The parity harness reads and writes two fixed /tmp directories, so two agents or two worktrees running it at the same time score one run's renders against another's - and the collision surfaces as a traceback, not as a refusal.
evidence: GOOSIE = Path('/tmp/goosie-renders') and CHROMIUM = Path('/tmp/playwright-renders') (testdata/parity.py:59-60) are global, unversioned and shared by every checkout on the machine, and --render truncates them in place. Measured at 02:10 on 2026-10-26: while this session's 100-site live sweep and another agent's `make parity` (pid 87939, `testdata/parity.py --render --render-chromium`) were both running, a read-only scoring pass in a third checkout died with `PIL.UnidentifiedImageError: cannot identify image file '/tmp/goosie-renders/grid/02-grid-alignment.png'` - a half-written PNG from the other process, rc 1, no verdict. The crash is the harmless outcome: the same race lets run A's Goosie renders be scored against run B's Chromium references, from different binaries, with nothing in the report saying which build produced either side. TASK-036 already established that a green `make parity` is one host's evidence; this is the same weakness one level down - within one host it is not even one BUILD's evidence. What closing needs: one render directory per run (mkdtemp, or a path derived from the binary's sha256), the chosen directory recorded in the JSON report next to each fixture, and a selftest case that proves two concurrent runs cannot read each other's files. Note the discipline that follows for agents: TASK-042 deliberately ran `python3 testdata/parity.py` without --render to avoid destroying evidence that other work was reading (its rule 9), which is right but invisible - nothing in the harness says the directory is somebody else's evidence. Same root, one more failure mode measured 2026-10-26 while integrating TASK-040: a mutation that makes a fixture stop rendering at all (rc 1, no PNG written) leaves the PREVIOUS run's PNG sitting at /tmp/goosie-renders/<fixture>.png, and `--render` then scores that stale image as if the current binary had produced it. Caught only because the good PNG was moved away by hand first - with it in place the mutated binary still reported 85/85 100%. The MISSING/exit-1 half of the corpus gate therefore depends on the shared directory being clean, which nothing in the harness enforces. Fixing this is the same change as the per-run directory: render into a fresh path and treat any pre-existing image for a fixture as not-this-run's evidence. CLOSED 2026-11-12 in e22d71f. `testdata/parity.py` gains `--workdir DIR`, which resolves to `DIR/goosie` + `DIR/chromium` and moves BOTH sides together (a private goosie root scoring against the shared Chromium root is still a borrowed corpus), and `--isolate`, the same thing with `tempfile.mkdtemp`; with neither flag the machine-global defaults are kept, which is what `scripts/run-parity.sh` (pre-generated references, `-skip-render`) and the CI job depend on. `render_goosie` and `render_chromium` now `out.unlink(missing_ok=True)` BEFORE invoking the producer, so the measured failure mode is gone: a binary that renders nothing leaves no image to inherit and the fixture comes back MISSING with rc 1. Provenance is recorded at both levels - `metadata.render_provenance` carries the binary path, its sha256, both roots and a `per_run_corpus` flag, and every fixture row carries `goosie_render`/`chromium_render`, so a PASS names the two files it was measured from. Writing the shared roots with a render flag prints a stderr NOTE saying that directory is another run's evidence and naming the isolation flags. Oracles: `testdata/parity_selftest.py` cases 6-8 (41 checks green, no browser) and gate `test/gatecheck/parity_harness_test.go:TestParityWorkdirIsAccepted` (qc:BR-264); catalog row BR-264 and `expectedCaseCount` 263 -> 264 move with it. Measured mutants, each restored: deleting the `out.unlink` turns case 7 red on three checks and its last line prints `[('PASS', None)]` - this defect's exact fraud path reproduced from source; deleting `global GOOSIE, CHROMIUM` turns case 8 red because the readers stay on the old root; renaming `--workdir` turns the gate red. Blast radius: `--render` on the shared roots scored 107/107 at 96.43% with gaps 4 fixtures / 6 bands, and `--isolate --render --render-chromium` rendering BOTH sides into a private corpus scored the identical numbers, so the new flags neither loosen the gate nor depend on a warm directory. Still open and unrelated to this mechanism: parity has never been measured on ubuntu-latest, which stays `GOOSIE-CIPARITY-001`.

summary: A document the source refused (4xx) is still rendered and scored as if it were the page, so the live harness labels a blocked site LAYOUT_EMPTY - 'the engine made nothing' and 'the site said no' share one label.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-005. TASK-039 put the refusal on stderr (`goosie: the source refused <url> with HTTP <status>; rendered <n> bytes of that refusal, not the page`, cmd/goosie/document_loader.go:455, oracle BR-190 with mutation M5 re-measured by the integrator: nipping the threshold to `>= 0` kills `TestGoosieScreenshotStaysSilentOnAnAcceptedDocument`). The harness half is not done: testdata/live-parity.py compares whatever Chromium and Goosie each painted and has no field for the HTTP status, so a 403 body scores as LAYOUT_EMPTY or LOW_COVERAGE. Measured in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1920Z-eef92ae7.json: 8 rows carry LAYOUT_EMPTY, and the sweep's own `goosie_diag` is where the refusal now lives, not in the label. What closing needs: capture the response status per page, add a REFUSED_BY_SOURCE label, and count how many of the current LAYOUT_EMPTY rows are actually refusals - until then the eight-page figure inside GOOSIE-LIVE-001 is an upper bound that mixes two causes. PARTIAL, measured 2026-10-26 against sweep 13 (`2026-10-26T0726Z-7f71648c`): 10 of the 100 rows are refusals (the source answered HTTP 401/403/404), spread across four labels - 6 of the 7 `LAYOUT_EMPTY` (apnews, nytimes, japantimes, reuters, etsy, newegg), 2 `UNFLAGGED` (the Wikipedia list URL and census.gov), 1 `LOW_COVERAGE` (docs.kernel.org, 404) and 1 `MISSING_REGIONS` (uniqlo) - so the LAYOUT_EMPTY family has two causes: zara is the only `LAYOUT_EMPTY` row that is not a refusal (it reports an uncaught script error). The Markdown report now names every one of those rows with its status under "Pages that are not engine measurements" (commit b253495), including the terminal-rung rows, and the harness selftest pins the section and its scoping. What still keeps this open: the status is recovered from `goosie_diag` by the report rather than carried as a first-class row field, and classify still has no `REFUSED_BY_SOURCE` rung, so label counts and the exit code still treat a refusal exactly like a layout result.

summary: A 20-32 px ink smudge in the top-left corner of Goosie's renders is counted by content_bands as a content band, so a page whose only Goosie output is that smudge reads as 'has content'.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-006. At ink_goosie=32 the vnexpress.net render (viewport 1280x1024) is a smudge inside (0,0)-(4,3) and nothing else; parity.content_bands treats its row range as a band, and the sweep recorded it as BLANK_OUTPUT only because the coverage ratio collapsed, not because the band was rejected. TASK-039 §5.5 measured what the smudge is (branch F) but did not root-cause which tile produces it, and §5.11.4 records that the probe needed is on the raster/frame side with a minimal fixture. What closing needs: a fixture that paints nothing but the corner, a statement of which of the two (uncovered tile, glyph-atlas bleed) it is, and a floor in the band metric that ignores a band of that size - the floor must be set from measurement, not tuned until the label goes away. CLOSED by TASK-046's localisation (adf2664, merged in 9754fda) on a mechanism shipped by TASK-044 (9e08c9d), and by the integrator's own re-measurement. This entry asked which of two causes it was - uncovered tile or glyph-atlas bleed - and the answer measured on this host is **neither**: with `raster.RasterizeTile` on an empty list over a fully covered tile the ink is 0, and the tile raster of the real list is pixel-identical to the headless PNG, so the ink is authored in the display list. The shape is two zero-size boxes at content (0,0) - `.sub-area` and `.nav-folder .ul-nav-folder li.has-submn .sub-more`, both `opacity: 0; visibility: hidden` - whose `box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.2)` ring strips survive into the origin tile: 4 cols x 5 rows = 20 px, and the colour arithmetic closes (`255*0.8^4 = 104`, `255*0.8^2 = 163`, `247*0.8^4 = 101`, `247*0.8^2 = 158` - exactly the values TASK-039 §5.5 recorded). They painted at full strength because `DisplayCmd.Opacity == 0` is the reserved 'unset -> opaque' sentinel (`internal/paint/cmd.go:151-154`). The third closing condition - a floor in the band metric - is dropped as unnecessary, measured not assumed: `parity.content_bands` returns **0 bands** for the 4x5 smudge in both the pre-fix and the merged binary (5 rows < MIN_BAND_HEIGHT 6, 20 px < MIN_INK 200), so no threshold was added and vnexpress stays BLANK_OUTPUT for the reason GOOSIE-LIVE-001 owns. The band premise was true one shape wider: an `opacity: 0` element with a 40x40 background put **1600 opaque px** on the page and produced **1 band** before the fix; integrator's own numbers with two binaries built here (headless 800x600 DPR 1, `parity.ink_mask`): bg-op0 1600 -> 0, shadow-op0 20 -> 0, a *visible* shadow control 20 -> 20 unchanged, empty 0 -> 0. Oracle: `test/paint/invisible_box_test.go` tagged BR-196, and both of its suppression cases go red when the merged guards are removed (see §8 of the task doc).

summary: An escaped quote inside an unquoted url() token opens a string that never closes, so every rule after it in the same stylesheet is dropped - the shape that hides vnexpress's tail rules and that the current parser only survives by luck when the sheet holds an even number of quote characters.
evidence: GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-003. CSS Syntax L3 4.3.8 makes a backslash escape the next byte anywhere in the token stream, so `\'` inside `url(...)` must not start a string. Goosie applies the escape-skip only in the `quote != 0` branch of the boundary scanners (internal/css/parser.go, parseRule's selector and declaration loops and parseBlockWithRules' statement loop), so outside a string the `'` of `\'` still opens one. Measured on a minimal file (one `.u{background-image:url(data:image/svg+xml;...\'26\'...)}` rule plus `.after{background:#0f0}` and a text node, viewport 400x300): Chromium computes `.u` width 120px and `.after` rgb(0,255,0) - both rules survive; eef92ae paints 2,806 ink px (both boxes gone, only the text), and da68c5b paints 16,325 (both boxes). This is a REGRESSION introduced by a9f6218, which added the inside-string skip. Second measurement, on vnexpress.net's own second inline <style> block (94,344 bytes, one line, 80 single quotes, 409 backslashes) with a `.ZZ{background:#0f0;width:120px;height:120px}` marker appended: da68c5b paints the marker (14,400 px), eef92ae paints nothing (0 px). The two builds differ only in whether an escaped quote closes a string, so the old one was right by accident - an even number of quote characters leaves the state balanced - and the new one is wrong for that shape. Both directions are real: on the whole vnexpress.net page ink went 32 -> 320,348 between the da68c5b and eef92ae sweeps, because a different sheet on that page has the odd-count shape. Why no gate saw it: no test under test/css contains an escaped quote inside a string or a url token, and BR-186's nine tests cover the raw-newline and escaped-newline halves only; the render corpus has no escaped-quote-in-url fixture, so `make parity` is 83/83 green across this change. What closing needs: the escape-skip in both states at every boundary scanner (including the lenient sites that never end at a newline, parser.go:1321, :1346, :1419, :1681, :1784 and SplitDeclarations), expectations taken from Chromium measurement rather than memory, a unit oracle for `url(...\'...\')`, a parity fixture whose tail rule disappears when the scanner mis-tracks state, and a mutation proof that the fixture kills the current behaviour. CLOSED by e3b8292. Fix: `startsEscape` is tested before the quote branches in every quote-tracking scan (parseRule's selector and body loops, parseBlockWithRules' at-prelude, at-block, statement and nested-rule scans, ExpandSingleNestedSelector, SplitDeclarations), so an escaped byte is consumed with its backslash in both states; the body loop tracks parens apart from braces and 4.3.9 stops a quote inside `url(...)` from opening a string at all. Verified here, not claimed: five oracles green, `go test -count=1 ./...` rc 0, `go vet -all ./...` rc 0, `go test ./internal/archtest/` rc 0, `make parity` 84/84 at average 96.13% with css-features/10 at 97.42% and 0 blank bands, and the gate-level mutation - the same fixture rendered by eef92ae - scores 78.61% FAIL with 5 blank bands and parity exit 1. Re-measured outcomes on the inputs that opened this defect: the marker sheet (vnexpress style#1 + tail rule) paints 14,400 px again instead of 0, and the minimal probe recovers both boxes (16,325 px). Still open, deliberately not folded in: escape *decoding* (Goosie keeps the backslashes in the value while Chromium computes `url("data:x'y")`), hex escapes like `\A`, and selector matching on an escaped quote (GOOSIE-CSSSELECT-001). None of them changes a pixel on the shapes measured here - Chromium computes `background-image: none` for the vnexpress-style URI too - so they stay recorded as debt rather than being fixed blind.

summary: A selector whose quoted value holds an escaped quote parses into the stylesheet but never matches, so the element keeps its unstyled box - the rule exists, the match does not.
evidence: GOOSIE-CSSSELECT-001. Measured 2026-10-26 on `.s[data-x="a\"b"]{background:#8e44ad;height:24px}` with `<div class="s" data-x='a"b'>`: Chromium computes the band 760x24 at rgb(142,68,173); Goosie paints no band at all. This is not the parser losing the rule - test/css/escaped_quote_test.go:TestEscapedQuoteInsideSelectorAttributeKeepsFollowingRules proves the rule and both its declarations survive (that half is BR-191) - so the loss is in selector matching, which still compares the raw text including the backslash. TASK-041 §7.6 already recorded 'selector text keeps the escape pair' as remaining debt; this is that debt with a measured page-level consequence. The render fixture css-features/10-escaped-quote-url.html deliberately uses an unescaped attribute value, so nothing in the corpus enshrines the wrong match. What closing needs: unescape the value when a selector is compiled (CSS Syntax L3 4.3.10 identifiers and 4.3.7 strings), one oracle per side (escaped quote, escaped space, hex escape like `\A`), and a fixture whose band only paints when the match works. CLOSED by 6005d14e (2026-11-12, BR-268). Decoding happens where the condition is compiled: `unquoteCSSValue` in internal/css/selector.go takes the payload covered by the string's own run (`quotedRunEnd` steps over every escape pair) and passes it to `DecodeEscapes`, replacing the `strings.Trim` cutset that ate the closing quote of exactly this defect's spelling. Unquoted values decode as identifiers (4.3.10), so an escaped space, a hex escape like `\41` (-> `A`) and a doubled backslash now match the strings Chromium names; text with no escapes is byte-identical, which is why no existing selector test moved. Two sibling scans were quote-blind for the same reason and now share that one primitive: `attrConditionEnd` (the `]` inside `[data-x="a]b"]` is one byte of the value, so that is a single condition matching `a]b` - measured) and the comma split in `splitSelectorListExact` + `css.splitSelectors` (the `,` inside `[data-x="a,b"]` is not a list separator; the old split handed the parser two broken selectors and lost the declarations). `validAttrCondition` now rejects bytes after a closing quote, because Chromium throws SyntaxError for `[data-x="a"b"]` and `[data-x="a\"b"c]`, where the binary on this defect's head cut the value down to `a"b` and matched an element its own text cannot name; an unterminated string still recovers at end of input and matches nothing (both branches measured). Eight oracles on three layers, every expectation measured with Playwright on 2026-11-12 against that document rather than written from spec memory: test/css/attr_selector_value_test.go (5: match table, absent-value table, throw table, comma-is-one-selector, rule keeps its declarations), test/style/attr_selector_value_test.go (2: the cascade paints the string's box and not the spelling's, including the `#8e44ad` of the opening measurement), test/js/attr_selector_value_test.go (1: a 15-result `querySelectorAll`/`matches` script that includes the throw). Mutation proof is pixel-level: a binary built from the pre-fix tree puts the five rule colours on the box holding the selector's SPELLING instead of the box holding the string, and loses #27ae60 and #c0392b entirely (0 px each). Fixture css-features/19-attr-selector-escaped-value.html scores 98.723% PASS (worst_region_iou 0.9766, coverage_ratio 0.9755, blank bands 0/0), corpus 108/108 at average 96.451%, floor 107 -> 108, known gaps unchanged at 4 fixtures / 6 bands; build, `go vet -all ./...`, `go test ./...`, `-race` on css/style/js, archtest, `make gate` and the gate suite all green on this host. Split off rather than folded in: the line-box gap the fixture's first version exposed is GOOSIE-INLINESTRUT-001, and escape decoding inside quoted `url()` payloads stays GOOSIE-CSSURLESCAPE-001.

summary: visibility:hidden and element opacity never reach the display list, so boxes the author hid are painted anyway; once the CSS string fix let vnexpress's stylesheet through, one hidden full-width overlay turned the whole page into a flat grey panel.
evidence: GOOSIE-VIS-001. Measured on this host 2026-10-26 with cmd/dump-paint on a four-box document (/tmp/vis-probe2.html): the frozen display list is [EXTENT 800x200, FILL (0,0,800,200), FILL (8,8,108,58), FILL (8,58,108,108)] - the box carrying 'opacity:0;visibility:hidden' is emitted, the box carrying only 'visibility:hidden' is emitted, the box carrying only 'opacity:0' is emitted, and only the 'display:none' box is correctly absent. Pixels agree: a 400x300 render of the same overlay holds exactly 79,509 #f7f7f7 pixels in all four variants, i.e. the hidden and the transparent case are indistinguishable from the plain one. Code reading: internal/style/style.go:2559 stores cs.Visibility and the cascade keeps it in style_diff.go:101, but the only consumer in the tree is internal/paint/builder_controls.go:466 (list markers); no box or text path consults it. Opacity does have a raster consumer (internal/raster/tile.go applyOpacity) yet the value arriving for this element is opaque, so either the computed style never carries it into paint or paint builds the box without it - the implementer has to say which. PAGE-LEVEL CONSEQUENCE, and this is what makes it P1 rather than a missing feature: vnexpress's '.wrap-all-menu{width:100%;float:left;background:#f7f7f7;position:absolute;top:calc(100% + 10px);opacity:0;visibility:hidden}' used to be dropped along with the rest of its stylesheet. After GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-003 closed at e3b8292 the rule is admitted, so the sweep at 2ca7889 records the page as BLANK_OUTPUT (coverage 0.0, ink 32, doc_height 691) where the sweep at eef92ae recorded LOW_COVERAGE (coverage 0.441, ink 320,348, doc_height 1625). Attribution was measured on one saved copy of the page (254,146 characters, rendered both with and without its <script> blocks) across three binaries: eef92ae PNG 316,893 B / ink 261,030, 72a11f8 PNG 224,125 B / ink 261,030, 2ca7889 PNG 4,837 B / ink 345,600 - the script-free column is byte-identical between the first two, which rules out TASK-039's script execution as the cause and points at the newly admitted CSS. The fix is NOT the reason to revert: on the same nine vnexpress sheets the parser now yields 882 rules where the pre-fix parser yielded 174, and a 120x120 marker rule appended to the end of the 94 KB sheet survives on main (14,400 ink px) but is lost on the pre-fix binary (0). Scope of the claim, narrowed after checking the code: the property is **not** inert. `internal/style/style.go:2577` stores it, `DefaultStyle()` gives `visible` at :689, and there are real consumers - `internal/layout/block.go:240` and :2436 (`hidden` skips contents and can size from `ContainIntrinsicHeight`) and `internal/paint/builder_box.go:83` (`hidden` stops the subtree walk) - plus tests `test/style/content_visibility_test.go:TestContentVisibilityProperties`, `TestContentVisibilitySingleIntrinsicSize` and `test/layout/anchor_test.go:TestContentVisibilityHiddenLayoutSizing`. What is missing is `auto`: every comparison in the tree is `== "hidden"`, so the value the cascade stores for `auto` is read nowhere and a document using `content-visibility: auto` behaves as if it said `visible`. **Correction kept on the record: the first draft of this entry, written before the grep above, said the field had no consumer and no test. That was false and is withdrawn here rather than quietly edited away.** Not measured against Chromium on this host, so no claim is made about which part of the `auto` contract (skipped rendering, contain-intrinsic-size swap, finding-in-page) matters most. What closing needs: a Chromium anchor for `auto` on a long page, then either the behaviour or an explicit scope statement in the roadmap.

summary: An inline element’s border is never painted at all: `paintBorders` sits behind a non-inline test, so inline boxes lose their borders instead of fragmenting them per line.
evidence: GOOSIE-INLINEBORDER-001 - reported by TASK-048 §6.1 and re-measured independently by the integrator on 2026-10-26 on my own document `/tmp/t48-res/inlineborder.html` (`div{width:300px;height:60px;margin:10px;background:rgba(200,0,0,.5)}` with `span{border:3px solid rgba(0,0,200,.5)}` around "two"). `cmd/dump-paint` emits **0** BORDER commands on main and **0** on the TASK-048 branch — the only BORDER in the engine’s output for a block border test appears for the block itself (`BORDER rect=(0,0,306,66)` in TASK-048’s §6.1 dump), never for an inline. Chromium paints the span’s border box: over my measured region Chromium holds 198 px of (113,63,163) — exactly `rgba(0,0,200,.5)` composited once over the block tint (227,127,127) — and Goosie holds none of that colour anywhere; Goosie’s only extra colours in the region are glyph antialiasing (125,70,70 / 68,38,38 / 191,107,107). Root is the same test that protects borders from the duplication in GOOSIE-INLINEBG-001: `paintBoxDecoration` runs `paintBorders` only when `computed.Display != style.DisplayInline`, so text runs (inline) cannot re-emit the element’s border — which is why no border duplication exists to register — but an inline element’s own border is dropped rather than fragmented one box per line, as CSS fragmentation requires. Blast radius: any page that draws a rule or a chip outline with `border` on an inline element (including `<a>`/`<abbr>`/`<code>` styling) loses it silently; invisible to the corpus because no fixture puts a border on an inline box. What closing needs: emit one border per inline fragment of an inline element (left/right strips only at the true start/end of the run, per css-text-decor L3 §4.6 analogue), an oracle counting BORDER commands per fragment, and a scored fixture. Needs a task. CLOSURE (SP-7, 2026-11-12): layout records per-line border-box fragments on Object.InlineFragments (internal/layout/inline.go finalizeInlineFragments, captured under the generating inline element by DOM parent in the positioning loop; inline borders are resolved at Block entry because inlineInto first runs inside the Block pass); paint emits one CmdBorder per fragment with top/bottom on every fragment and the inline-start/inline-end edges only on the first/last (internal/paint/builder_borders.go paintBorderFragment, builder_box.go paintBoxDecoration). Oracles: test/layout/inline_border_fragment_test.go (fragment count/order/edge expansion) and test/paint/inline_border_fragment_test.go (one border per fragment, start/end mask). Three mutants killed: M1 suppress guard, M2 four-edge-per-fragment, M3 union-rect-only. Fixture borders/04-inline-fragment.html scores 98.86% PASS with no blank band, MIN_SCORED_FIXTURES 105 -> 106, the prior 105 fixtures byte-identical, corpus gaps unchanged 4 fixtures / 6 bands. Deferred (spec section 8): inline outline, border-image and border-radius on fragments, RTL pixel sign-off.

summary: A live-sweep row is not reproducible even when the binary is bit-identical: what a page’s row records depends on how far that page’s own scripts got at capture time, so the same URL on the same engine yields a 4,368 px document in one sweep and a 34,795 px one in the next.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-009 - measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while attributing sweep 7 (`docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-26T0011Z-741fdd37`, build source `741fdd37`) against sweep 6 (`2026-10-25T2212Z-4302e3cb`, build source `9754fda4`). The engine side is provably deterministic: three consecutive `./bin/goosie -backend headless -width 1280 -height 1024 -dpr 1 -screenshot -url https://www.walmart.com/` runs on this host produced **one** PNG hash (`6472fedefe08…`, 500,177 B) and **one** ink count (1,138,344 non-white px) with rc 0 and the same stderr each time. Yet walmart’s row says `ink_goosie` 1,077,200 with `doc_height` 4,368 in sweep 6 and 519,333 with `doc_height` 34,795 in sweep 7 — an 8× document height and a 52% ink swing on a URL whose HTML is byte-stable (three `curl` fetches: 450,325 B, sha256 prefix `14b086e65f377ad7`, identical). The page’s own script state, not the engine and not the HTML, is what moved. Scale of it, from the same two sweeps: **84 of 94** compared rows have byte-identical `ink_goosie` across two different builds, and every row where both `ink_goosie` and `ink_chromium` are identical also has `pct_exact` delta **exactly 0.00** (apnews.com, datatracker.ietf.org, doc.rust-lang.org/book and std, docs.kernel.org, docs.python.org ×3, en.wikipedia ×3 …) — so the metric is reproducible and the noise is entirely in what the reference and the page contribute at capture time. The movers confirm the direction: nld.com.vn `pct_exact` −27.39 with `ink_goosie` −0.1% and `ink_chromium` **+391%**; de.wikipedia −6.08 with ink Goosie identical and Chromium +42%; zingnews `ink_goosie` **+68.8%** (an engine change that only *removes* fills cannot add ink, so this is page state); two of six label flips (de/zh.wikipedia) happen with Goosie’s ink identical to the byte. Consequence for how a sweep may be read: a label flip or a `pct_exact` move is an engine result only when the engine’s own numbers moved too — which is why sweep 7 attributes exactly **one** of its six flips to code (see GOOSIE-INLINEBG-001’s note) and the rest to capture state. Not the same defect: GOOSIE-LIVE-004 (a row can read OK while the pixels are nowhere near each other), GOOSIE-LIVE-007 (FETCH_FAILED is decided on Chromium’s side — sweep 7 proves it again with bestbuy.com’s `TimeoutError: Page.goto: Timeout 30000ms`, where Goosie never got a turn), GOOSIE-LIVE-008 (report naming). What closing needs: pin the page state the row is allowed to depend on (wait for network idle plus a settled script-error count, or capture `doc_height` twice and refuse to score an unstable page), and record which of the two the row was taken with. Needs a task. Sweep 7 also brought its own repeated-pass noise floor back tighter than sweep 5/6 had it: 12 sites, 10 comparable, max |delta_pct_exact| **0.67**, max |delta_coverage| 0.077, **0** label flips. Read together that is the point of this entry - the spread on *static* pages is well under a point, while the pages that moved between sweeps moved 6 to 27 points, and every one of those movers has a reference- or script-side number that moved with it. A sweep's own repeated pass therefore cannot detect the instability this entry describes: it re-renders the same pages inside one capture window, where the page state is already fixed.

summary: The one non-test caller of the unchecked paint entry point is a shipped diagnostic: `cmd/dump-paint` paints geometry the engine refused to validate, and no test covers any `cmd/dump-*` binary at all.
evidence: GOOSIE-DIAGPAINT-001 - found by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while using `cmd/dump-paint` as a probe for TASK-048. Scope of the claim, measured rather than assumed: a repo-wide search for `Session.Paint(` and `PaintChecked(` outside tests yields 20 shipped call sites, 19 of them `PaintChecked` and exactly one raw `Paint(1)` - `cmd/dump-paint/main.go:28`. Everything the product runs (`cmd/goosie/*`, `cmd/goosie-headless`) is on the checked path, so this is not a user-facing bypass; it is a diagnostic an operator points at a file. Why it still matters: `AGENTS.md` "Untrusted Input" states binaries that touch untrusted input must call `Session.PaintChecked`, never `Paint`, and this binary reads an HTML file the operator supplies - which is untrusted input by that definition - and it is also the tool the QA registry now cites as evidence in catalog rows (BR-198 quotes its fill list, GOOSIE-VIS-001 and TASK-048 do the same), so a probe that skips the geometry gate can show commands a shipped build would never emit. The guard gap is separately real: `test/entrypoints/limits_test.go` builds and runs only `goosie-headless` and `goosie` (its six tests: invalid viewport, oversized document, valid document, screenshot invalid viewport, screenshot valid, oversized input) - searching the whole `test/` tree for `cmd/dump-paint` finds only two prose comments in `test/paint/inline_background_repaint_test.go:18,287`, no test. What closing needs: `dump-paint` (and a check over the other `cmd/dump-*`/`cmd/debug-*` binaries) to take `PaintChecked` and print the refusal on stderr with a non-zero rc, plus a source-level or process-level guard so a future diagnostic cannot silently re-add the unchecked call. Not measured: whether any of the other diagnostics admit input before parsing; this entry does not claim they do not. SECOND DEFECT OF THE SAME TOOL, measured 2026-10-26 while validating TASK-049: `cmd/dump-paint` prints only FILL, BORDER and TEXT lines, so it cannot see `CmdGradient`, `CmdRadialGradient` or `CmdImage` at all. That blind spot is why the anonymous-block gradient re-emission - three gradient rects `(0,0,300,76) (0,0,300,18) (0,38,300,56)` where Chromium has one - looked like nothing in the dump: TASK-049 had to read the display list through `paint.Builder` inside a Go test to see it (its 1.2). Registry rows written before this note (BR-198, GOOSIE-VIS-001) quote dump-paint fill lists as if they were the whole list; they are a projection. Closing this entry must therefore do two things, not one: switch the binary to `PaintChecked` AND print every command kind the tile path honours, otherwise the next gradient or image defect is again invisible to the only diagnostic an operator runs.

summary: A quoted `url("…")` whose payload contains `)` is cut at the first `)`, so inline-SVG backgrounds that use `rgb()`/`rgba()` colours lose the layer entirely while Chromium paints them; the computed value itself is wrong, not just the pixels.
evidence: GOOSIE-CSSURLPAREN-001 - found by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while checking a claim TASK-049 handed up ("Goosie never paints background-image"). That claim is FALSIFIED, and the real defect is narrower: measured with /tmp/bgimg-probe/variants5.html (four 100x20 bands, `cmd/goosie-headless` 120x90 DPR 1 against a Playwright capture of the same file), counting exact (0,0,255) px per band - Chromium paints ALL FOUR forms at 2,000 px; Goosie paints the two forms whose SVG carries a `%230000ff` colour at 2,000 px each and the two forms whose SVG carries `fill='rgb(0,0,255)'` at 0 px. Base64 forms paint too (svg;base64 Goosie 1,493 vs Chromium 1,455; png;base64 Goosie 1,458 vs Chromium 1,392 - the small deltas are tile-repeat seam rounding, a separate question). The corpus proves the same from the other side: colors/03-opacity.html carries an inline SVG background written with `%23ccc` and paints 27,314 px of (204,204,204) in Goosie against Chromium's 28,502, which is why no fixture is red today. MECHANISM, located by reading the computed value rather than guessing it: a throwaway cascade probe (run 2026-10-26, then deleted) printed `style.ComputedStyle.BackgroundImage` for each form - for the working form it is the full 140-char URI, for the broken one it is `data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='20' height='20'><rect width='20' height='20' fill='rgb(0,0,255` at 133 chars, i.e. the string STOPS at the first `)`. So the cut is in the *value re-scan*, not in the tokenizer: `internal/css/parser.go:1311,1891` already honour 4.3.9 (a quote inside `url(…)` is not a string start), but `internal/style/style.go:4655 extractBackgroundURL` re-extracts the payload with `strings.IndexByte(rest, ')')` (`:4662`) and only strips the quotes *after* that cut (`:4667`), so `url("…rgb(0,0,255)…")` comes back as `"…rgb(0,0,255` - exactly the 133 chars the probe printed. Searching `internal/` for that pattern found FIVE extraction sites: `style.go:4662`; `internal/css/border_image.go:86 borderImageURL`; `internal/engine/limits.go:1013 absolutizeCSSURLs`, which cuts and then re-emits the tail as new text, so a fetched sheet's quoted data URI is truncated *and* rewritten; `internal/engine/imports.go:122 importRef`; and `internal/engine/engine.go:706`, which is already quote-aware (`:698-705`) and is the reference for what the shared scanner must do. Only the first is proven by pixels today; TASK-050 is written against all five, and `internal/engine/limits.go:944 decodeDataImageURL` then faithfully percent-unescapes a URI that is no longer valid XML, so `imgdec.DecodeSVGAt` (`internal/engine/engine.go:1245`) fails and `obj.BgImage` is never set (`:1251`). Note `internal/paint/builder_background.go:92` DOES read `obj.BgImage`, so the paint layer is not the gap; TASK-049 named the wrong layer. Blast radius: `rgb()`/`rgba()` inside an inline SVG is one of the two idioms sites actually write (the other is `%23` hex, which works), so placeholder art, chevrons and gradient-on-SVG backgrounds vanish silently - and unlike a refused document this prints no diagnostic anywhere. What closing needs: the tokenizer must consume a quoted url up to its terminating quote (and reject unbalanced parens only in the unquoted form), an oracle asserting `BackgroundImage` byte-for-byte for a payload containing `)`, `(`, `%`, `#` and `'`, plus a scored fixture whose SVG background uses `rgba()`; and the falsified upstream claim should be corrected in TASK-049 rather than left standing. Priority note: this adds a sixth open P0/P1 entry, which the rc-sweep gate reads - it belongs at P1 because a shipped document's computed style is provably wrong, not because one layer is prettier. RE-MEASURED on main a5c5424 the same day, independently of the first probe: `cmd/goosie-headless -in /tmp/bgimg-probe/variants5.html -width 120 -height 90 -dpr 1` counts (0,0,255) px per band `[2000, 2000, 0, 0]`, while a Playwright capture of the identical file counts `[2000, 2000, 2000, 2000]` and keeps the whole payload in the computed value (lengths 147/142/150/145). So the discriminator is a `)` in the payload - not `;utf8`, not quoting: k1 (unquoted, `%230000ff`) paints and k3 (unquoted, `rgb(0,0,255)`) does not. Owner is now TASK-050 (spec `docs/tasks/TASK-050-CSS-URL-PAREN.md`, implementer dispatched 2026-10-26). CLOSED 2026-10-26 by TASK-050, merged at 6edb7e3 (implementation f171d6c, registration 8f58aa8), cases BR-211/BR-212. Fix: one shared scanner `internal/css/url.go` (`ScanURL`/`ScanURLAt`/`IndexURL`) that follows CSS Syntax L3 4.3.9 - a quoted payload runs to its matching quote and the token ends at the following `)`; an unquoted payload is read with balanced-paren depth - replaces the flat cut at SIX sites, not five: the five listed above plus `ParseBorderImageShorthand` in `internal/css/border_image.go`, found during the audit because it rejoined `strings.Fields` tokens around a quote-blind `strings.Contains(")")` and truncated a shorthand border-image the same way. summary: `Runtime.CheckIntersections` calls `entry.target.Export()` while holding `Runtime.mu`; exporting a node wrapper invokes its enumerable `shadowRoot`/`parentNode` getters, which call back into the runtime and try to take the same non-reentrant mutex, so any page that registers an IntersectionObserver deadlocks `NewSession` forever - the browser never finishes loading and a screenshot run is killed at its 120 s harness timeout.

LOCATION, from a SIGQUIT goroutine dump of the merged build on getbootstrap (saved /tmp/t50-hang.err, 49 KB): goroutine 1 is `[sync.Mutex.Lock]` in `js.(*Runtime).jsGetShadowRoot` (internal/js/shadow_dom.go:120) called from `setupDOM.func56` (internal/js/js.go:1168) through a goja property getter, called from goja `Object.Export`, called from `js.(*Runtime).CheckIntersections` (internal/js/intersection.go:311), from `engine.(*Session).Reflow` (internal/js/../engine/engine.go:1414), from `engine.NewSession` (engine.go:516), from cmd/goosie/document_loader.go:437 - i.e. the load path, not the screenshot driver.
